bug_description.normalized: The staged 113-byte witness is accepted as a DEX 035 file, and `dex_get_header()` materializes header fields that make `dex_parse()` treat bytes 0x20..0x3f of the same buffer as `class_def[0]`. That overlapping entry yields `class_data_offset = 0x0a`, so `dex_parse()` decodes class-data counts from offsets 0x0a..0x11 and obtains `static_fields_size = 0xffffffff` with cumulative `uleb128_size = 8`. Exact witness bytes 0x12..0x68 then drive 43 successful `load_encoded_field()` iterations until the next call starts at offset 105. `load_encoded_field()` only checks that an 8-byte window exists from the original start; its first unbounded `read_uleb128()` consumes five `0xff` bytes, but the second unbounded `read_uleb128()` begins at offset 110 with only three in-bounds bytes left, and `read_uleb128()` reads the missing fourth continuation byte at offset 113. The patch semantically fixes this by replacing the remaining unbounded DEX ULEB128 decodes with bounded reads and explicit error handling, but Stage 02 only has vulnerable-run evidence and does not validate fixed-image resolution.

source.value_from: The source consumes the 113-byte staged witness stored at `poc` (sha256 `393055ae72b3deae6bba6656cda043a1ee6aaa7b7ded13d30c45ddd2dfe6efad`), which is the same fuzzer-provided buffer that reproduced the saved ASan crash.
source.description: `dex_get_header()` is the first project parser statement that materializes the attacker-controlled buffer as a DEX header, creating the header fields that later steer `dex_parse()` into the overlapping class-def region.

root_cause.description: `load_encoded_field()` launches the second variable-length decode after the first one has already advanced `current_size`, but it performs no remaining-length validation and passes no end pointer into `read_uleb128()`. The patch replaces this exact call site with `read_uleb128_bounded(..., data_end, &current_size, &error)` and aborts on `error`.

sink.description: During the second ULEB128 decode, the fourth continuation-byte fetch dereferences offset 113, one byte past the 113-byte heap-backed fuzz input, producing the observed heap-buffer-overflow read.

tainted_value_origin.description: The first concrete attacker-derived parser state is the header pair `class_defs_size = 2` and `class_defs_offset = 0x20`, which later authorizes parsing a class-def table from bytes 0x20..0x5f of the same 113-byte buffer.

parser_admitted.description: After `dex_get_header(block_data, block->size)` accepts the witness magic `dex\n035\0`, `module_load()` dispatches the same buffer into `dex_parse()`. The saved ASan stack confirms the vulnerable path stays in `dex_parse -> load_encoded_field -> read_uleb128`.

coarse_trace.summary: The 113-byte witness passes the DEX 035 admission checks, and header materialization exposes `class_defs_size = 2` and `class_defs_offset = 0x20`.
`dex_parse()` accepts the header-declared class-def table, reads `class_def[0]` from overlapping bytes 0x20..0x3f, and obtains `class_data_offset = 0x0a`.
The parser decodes class-data counts at offsets 0x0a..0x11, gets `static_fields_size = 0xffffffff`, and exact witness bytes 0x12..0x68 advance the static-fields walk to `start_offset = 105`.
The crashing call passes the fixed 8-byte `fits_in_dex` precheck, then the first unchecked ULEB128 consumes five bytes and leaves the second unchecked decode starting at offset 110.
The second ULEB128 stays on the continuation-byte path for the last three in-bounds `0xff` bytes and overruns the heap buffer when it fetches the missing fourth continuation byte at offset 113.

fine_trace.note: The 113-byte staged witness is large enough for `dex_header_t` and starts with `dex\n035\0`, so this cast lets later code read header fields directly from attacker-controlled bytes. In the witness, offsets 0x60..0x63 decode to `class_defs_size = 2` and 0x64..0x67 decode to `class_defs_offset = 0x20`.

Using the header fields from step 1, the parser checks whether two `class_id_item_t` entries starting at offset 0x20 fit inside the 113-byte buffer. `0x20 + 2 * sizeof(class_id_item_t) = 0x60`, so the guard passes and authorizes parsing `class_def[0]` from bytes 0x20..0x3f.

fine_trace.code:
class_id_item_t* class_id_item = (class_id_item_t*) (
        dex->data +
        dex_header->class_defs_offset +
        i * sizeof(class_id_item_t));
fine_trace.note: On the first class-def iteration (`i == 0`), this statement materializes `class_def[0]` from bytes 0x20..0x3f, which overlap the header. The dword at offsets 0x38..0x3b becomes `class_data_offset = 0x0a`.

Because `class_data_offset != 0`, the parser enters the class-data block. The 16-byte guard passes because offsets 0x0a..0x19 lie within the 113-byte witness, so the parser proceeds to decode the four leading class-data counts from that region.

Bytes 0x0a..0x0e are `ff ff ff ff ff`, so the unbounded helper consumes five bytes, advances `uleb128_size` to 5, and after cast to `uint32_t` stores `static_fields_size = 0xffffffff` as the static-fields loop bound.

Bytes 0x0f, 0x10, and 0x11 are each `0x20`, so these three decodes each consume one byte and set `instance_fields_size = 32`, `direct_methods_size = 32`, and `virtual_methods_size = 32`. The cumulative `uleb128_size` becomes 8, so the first encoded-field parse will start at offset `0x0a + 8 = 0x12`.

The static-fields walk starts at offset 0x12. In the exact witness, bytes 0x12..0x68 form 43 successful encoded-field records: 42 two-byte records and one three-byte record at offsets 0x26..0x28 (`00 ff 20`). Their returned sizes add 87 bytes, moving `uleb128_size` from 8 to 95 so the next call uses `start_offset = 0x0a + 95 = 105`.

For the crashing call, `start_offset = 105` (`0x69`), so this fixed precheck succeeds because bytes 0x69..0x70 are the last eight in-bounds bytes of the witness. The guard reasons only about the original 8-byte window and does not reserve bytes for the second variable-length decode after the first one advances `current_size`.

At `start_offset = 105`, bytes 0x69..0x6d are `ff ff ff ff ff`, so the first unbounded decode consumes five bytes, stores `field_idx_diff = 0xffffffff`, and leaves `current_size = 5`. The second decode will therefore start at offset 110 (`0x6e`) with only three in-bounds bytes left.

Root cause. The second decode reuses the advanced `current_size` and starts at offset 110, but the caller performs no remaining-length check and passes no end pointer into `read_uleb128()`. The patch replaces this exact call with `read_uleb128_bounded(..., data_end, &current_size, &error)` and returns 0 when `error` is set.

Inside that second decode, bytes 0x6e, 0x6f, and 0x70 are all `0xff`, so the continuation-byte branches remain taken and line 241 attempts a fourth fetch at offset 113 (`0x71`). That dereference is one byte past the 113-byte heap buffer, matching the saved ASan `heap-buffer-overflow` READ of size 1 in `read_uleb128 -> load_encoded_field -> dex_parse`.

poc.trigger: The staged 113-byte witness `poc` (sha256 `393055ae72b3deae6bba6656cda043a1ee6aaa7b7ded13d30c45ddd2dfe6efad`) reproduces the saved ASan crash. It is admitted as DEX 035, yields `class_data_offset = 0x0a`, decodes `static_fields_size = 0xffffffff`, consumes exact bytes 0x12..0x68 across 43 prior `load_encoded_field()` iterations to reach `start_offset = 105`, and then overruns the buffer when the second unchecked ULEB128 fetches the missing fourth continuation byte at offset 113.

format.name: Witness-specific 113-byte DEX 035 file
format.contract: Stage-02 witness contract: the candidate must be byte-for-byte identical to the staged 113-byte `poc` file (sha256 `393055ae72b3deae6bba6656cda043a1ee6aaa7b7ded13d30c45ddd2dfe6efad`). The staged source and runtime artifacts do not justify a broader minimal contract, because bytes 0x12..0x68 determine the 43 earlier encoded-field sizes that place the crashing `load_encoded_field()` call at `start_offset = 105`.
